# Editorial: Congruence Equation

*Codeforces Round 460 (Div. 2), problem E*

Trying all integers from $1$ to $x$ is too slow to solve this problem. So we need to find out some features of that given equation.

Because we have $a^{p-1} \equiv 1 \quad (\textrm{mod}\;p)$ when $p$ is a prime, it is obvious that $a^z \; \textrm{mod} \; p$ falls into a loop and the looping section is $p-1$. Also, $z \; \textrm{mod} \; p$ has a looping section $p$. We can try to list a chart to show what $n \cdot a^n$ is with some specific $i, j$. (In the chart shown below, $n$ is equal to $i \cdot (p-1) + j$)

Proof for the chart shown above: For a certain $i, j$, we can see that n \\cdot a^n \\bmod p = ((i \\cdot (p-1) + j) \\bmod p) \\c
